dedupe_keys.name: seasfire cube global analysis ready data cube for seasonal fire modelling

description: The SeasFire Cube is a global, analysis-ready spatiotemporal data cube for modelling seasonal wildfire occurrence and burned area and their links to climate and human drivers. Version 0.4 of 26 September 2024 covers 2001 to 2021 at 8-day time steps and 0.25 degree resolution with 54 variables: ERA5 meteorology, MODIS vegetation indices, climate indices, Copernicus Emergency Management Service fire danger indices, GPW population density, burned area from GFED, GWIS and ESA FireCCI, and fire emissions. It was made by researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry, the National Observatory of Athens and Harokopio University of Athens in the SeasFire project funded by ESA's Future EO-1 programme. The cube is accessible as free Zarr downloads on Zenodo (two files, about 43.9 GB) under CC BY 4.0, with a tutorial repository on GitHub. Caveats: it stops in 2021, the coarse grid hides local asset exposure, and variables inherit their source products' gaps and biases. It supports hazard exposure analysis and forecasting of wildfire risk to power lines, roads and green infrastructure, and training of machine-learning fire models; related records are EFFIS and ERA5.
